subject.title: Transcript redaction corrupts Anthropic/Bedrock reasoning signatures (AIza/LTAI false positive), causing persistent replay_invalid

question: For provider-minted signed-thinking fields, should OpenClaw preserve structurally valid opaque replay tokens even when their bytes contain credential-shaped substrings?
rationale: The current tests deliberately redact credential-shaped provider signature fields, but the report shows that policy can corrupt real opaque replay tokens; maintainers need to choose the transcript redaction boundary before an automated repair changes it.

options.title: Scoped Structural Preservation
options.body: Preserve validated opaque signatures only in known provider signed-thinking fields while leaving arbitrary text, missing-route fields, and malformed payloads redacted.

options.title: Pattern-Only Hardening
options.body: Make fixed-case vendor prefixes and boundaries stricter but keep the current idempotent-redaction requirement for provider signatures.

options.title: Send-Side Recovery Only
options.body: Drop visibly corrupted signatures on Bedrock/Anthropic send and rely on repair/recovery without changing transcript-redaction preservation.

recommendation.title: Scoped Structural Preservation
recommendation.body: Preserve validated opaque signatures only in known provider signed-thinking fields while leaving arbitrary text, missing-route fields, and malformed payloads redacted.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved choice is a secret-redaction/security boundary, and the strongest history signal for that boundary is repeated ownership of src/logging/redact.ts hardening.
